source_caption:
The Truman Show works so well because Jim Carrey doesn’t play Truman like a man trapped in a sci-fi concept — he plays him like someone slowly realizing his entire life has been edited for an audience. Every smile starts to feel suspicious, every routine begins to crack, and the comedy quietly turns into one of cinema’s most haunting portraits of freedom.

The Truman Show (1998), directed by Peter Weir, starring Jim Carrey, Laura Linney, Ed Harris. A brilliant and deeply human satire about reality, control, and identity, following a man who discovers that his entire world may have been built around him.

source_details.title: The Truman Show
source_details.synopsis: The Truman Show is a 1998 American comedy-drama film directed by Peter Weir, and written and co-produced by Andrew Niccol. It stars Jim Carrey as Truman Burbank, a man who is unaware that he is living on a colossal soundstage, and that his life is the subject of a reality television show. The film's supporting cast includes Laura Linney, Ed Harris, Noah Emmerich, Natascha McElhone, Holland Taylor, and Paul Giamatti. Niccol's original spec script was more of a science-fiction thriller, with the story set in New York City. Producer Scott Rudin purchased the script and set up production at Paramount Pictures. Brian De Palma was to direct before Weir signed on as director, making the film for $6
